senses.gloss: picking, biting; chiselling.—נ׳ עינים putting out the eyes. Pesik. Aḥăré, p. 168ᵇ; Lev. R. s. 20; Tanḥ. Vaëthḥ. 1; Koh. R. to VIII, 17.—נ׳ אבנים chiselling of stones.
units: Sot. 46ᵇ.—Esp. the picking or biting done by birds, snakes &c., traces of biting.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 35a:8">Ab. Zar. 35ᵃ</cite> (<cite ref="N00519"><he>נחש</he></cite>) <he>משום נ׳</he> because a serpent may have touched it.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 8:3:33">Y. Ter. VIII, 46ᵃ</cite> top <he>דג נ׳</he> a fish showing traces of bites; a. fr.—Pl. <he>נִיקּוּרִים</he>, <he>נִיקּוּרִין</he>, <cite ref="N00763"><he>נִקּ׳</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Terumot 8:6">Ter. VIII, 6</cite> <he>נִיקּוּרֵי תאנים וכ׳</he> figs &c. which appear to have been bitten at (possibly by snakes); <cite ref="Tosefta Terumot 7:16">Tosef. ib. VII, 16</cite> <he>נ׳ תבשיל וכ׳</he> a dish &c. showing traces of bites.

Kidd. 80ᵃ, sq. נמצאו נ׳ נ׳ וכ׳ the dough shows that it has been pecked at (by chickens); a. fr.—Esp. niḳḳurin, laws concerning food suspected of having been touched by snakes. Y. Ter. l. c.; v. אֲפַּךְ; a. fr.

senses.gloss: pl. worm-eaten cloth, shreds. Midr. Sam. ch. XXII (some ed. ניקוד׳, corr. acc.); Yalk. ib. 129, v. בְּרוּקְלֵי.
